before_row.title: Level-one global-basis transition polynomials in the symmetric-group convention
before_row.axiom_use: Inherits the axiom of choice through [[thm-the-basic-representation-global-basis-is-unitriangular-in-the-partition-basis]] (and hence through [[thm-the-empty-component-is-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-zero]]) for the decomposition of the Fock space into highest-weight components; the definition of the polynomials themselves and the pairing are choice-free. Consumers must carry the same assumption while it is used.
before_row.statement:
Use the LINEAR model J M_mu=|mu-prime> and its transported action/bar/chart. Let M_sym=J^-1 V(Lambda0). For restricted lambda define G_sym(lambda)=J^-1 G_QG(lambda-prime), with G_sym(lambda)≡M_lambda mod qF0_sym. Write G_sym(lambda)=Σ_mu d_(lambda,mu)(q) M_mu. Then d_(lambda,lambda)=1; offdiagonal coefficients lie in qZ[q], vanish unless mu DOMINATES lambda and has the same e-core and full reflected residue weight. Precisely d_(lambda,mu)=D_QG(mu-prime,lambda-prime), where QG D has standard rows and lower columns. This is a lower-to-lower linear model relabeling, distinct from semilinear transpose/adjoint formulas and same-model Mullineux.

Define the ambient polarization B(M_mu,M_nu)=delta_(mu,nu). In each finite full weight space let D_rect have columns G_sym(lambda) for the restricted/basic labels and rows ALL standard shapes of that weight. H=D_rect^t D_rect is its nondegenerate FIELD Gram matrix. The basic upper vectors are G_sym^*(lambda)=Σ_mu (D_rect H^-1)_(mu,lambda) M_mu^*, where M_mu^* denotes the ambient orthonormal dual frame; these are coordinates in the ambient space, not a 'standard basis of the basic module'. Thus e_(lambda,mu)=(D_rect H^-1)_(mu,lambda) is in Q(q), and need not be Laurent integral or polynomial. The restricted graded A-dual lattice of the basic LOWER A-span is free weightwise and perfectly paired with it by the upper basis, as supplied by the exact upper-duality theorem; this does not imply lower-A selfduality, an A-unit H, or full algebraic duality in infinite rank. Upper bar is the adjoint bar psi^vee with its own dual infinity chart and the exact weighted upper operators, not ordinary lower bar. In contrast, the FULL ambient upper matrix is D_full^-t and is Laurent integral since D_full is unitriangular. At e2, restricted lambda11 has G_sym11=M11+qM2, so G_sym^*11=(M11+qM2)/(1+q²), an explicit non-A ambient-coordinate example. No specialization of d to decomposition numbers is asserted without the separate correct Hecke parameter hypotheses.
before_row.strategy: The actual QG ambient lower globalization plus its integral/basic-lift inclusion proves existence, uniqueness, polynomiality, weights/core and dominance; apply J without changing q. Transposition reverses the dominance inequalities and conjugates the core, proving the support direction. The node-cube supplier proves the exact ambient polarization: for an added i-node, N_l+N_r=N_i(smaller)−1, so (F_i lambda,mu)=q^N_r=(lambda,q^-1 K_i E_i mu); E follows by the swapped formula, and toral/divided compatibility follows by powers. The basic restriction is normalized nondegenerate by its simple highest-module form theorem. Finite inverse Gram therefore gives unique upper vectors with (G_a,G_b^*)=delta_ab; it is a FIELD inverse and D_rect need not be square. Weightwise A-dual basis/perfectness is separately the actual restricted graded upper-duality theorem, obtained from finite inverse Gram even with nonunit determinant. Its adjoint bar/charts/operators transfer through J and are not inferred from lower-bar invariance. The e2 example follows directly from the source-normalized lower G2; denominator1+q² is not a unit in Z[q±], proving the necessity of rational ambient coordinates. For the full ambient case triangular D_full has polynomial inverse, so its field dual matrix D_full^-t has Laurent integer entries. This establishes all promised genuine lower/upper comparison clauses while correcting the original nonexistent rectangular inverse and lower/adjoint model conflation.

after_row.title: Level-one global-basis transition polynomials in the symmetric-group convention
after_row.axiom_use: Inherits the axiom of choice through [[thm-the-basic-representation-global-basis-is-unitriangular-in-the-partition-basis]] (and hence through [[thm-the-empty-component-is-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-zero]]) for the decomposition of the Fock space into highest-weight components; the definition of the polynomials themselves and the pairing are choice-free. Consumers must carry the same assumption while it is used.
after_row.statement:
Work in the linear symmetric-group model of
[[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]]: the
$\mathbb{Q}(q)$-linear isomorphism $J M_\mu = |\mu'\rangle$, the transported
action, bar and $A_0$ standard chart $(F_0)_{\mathrm{sym}}$, and the weight
$\operatorname{wt}(M_\mu) = \Lambda_0 - \sum_i m_i(\mu)\alpha_i$, with
$A = \mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]$.

**The basic module and its lower basis.** Let
$M_{\mathrm{sym}} := J^{-1}V(\Lambda_0) = J^{-1}M_{\mathrm{QG}}$ be the
transported highest-weight module of the vacuum; by
[[thm-restricted-partition-component-is-the-basic-crystal-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]
its crystal is the $e$-restricted component and its labels are the $e$-restricted
partitions. For an $e$-restricted $\lambda$ define
$$G_{\mathrm{sym}}(\lambda) := J^{-1}G_{\mathrm{QG}}(\lambda'),$$
where $G_{\mathrm{QG}}(\mu)$ is the lower global (canonical) basis element of
the Fock space at the standard vector $|\mu\rangle$
([[thm-the-basic-representation-global-basis-is-unitriangular-in-the-partition-basis]]).
Then $G_{\mathrm{sym}}(\lambda) \equiv M_\lambda \bmod q\,(F_0)_{\mathrm{sym}}$
and the family $\{G_{\mathrm{sym}}(\lambda)\}$ is the transported lower global
basis of $M_{\mathrm{sym}}$, indexed by the restricted labels. Define the
**level-one transition polynomials in the symmetric-group convention** by the
finite weightwise expansion
$$G_{\mathrm{sym}}(\lambda) = \sum_\mu d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)\, M_\mu ,$$
the sum being over the partitions $\mu$ of the weight of $\lambda$.

**Ambient polarization and ambient upper coordinates.** Define the ambient
polarization by $B(M_\mu,M_\nu) = \delta_{\mu\nu}$ on the standard basis, a
symmetric nondegenerate bilinear form on each finite weight space. Fix a weight
$w$ and let $V_w$ be the (finite-dimensional) weight space of
$F_{\mathrm{sym}}$; let $D_{\mathrm{rect}}$ be the matrix with columns the
coordinate vectors of $G_{\mathrm{sym}}(\lambda)$ for the finitely many
$e$-restricted $\lambda$ of weight $w$, and rows the **standard** shapes
$M_\mu$, $\mu$ of weight $w$; let
$$H := D_{\mathrm{rect}}^{\mathsf{t}}\, D_{\mathrm{rect}} , \qquad G_{\mathrm{sym}}^*(\lambda) := \sum_\mu \bigl(D_{\mathrm{rect}}H^{-1}\bigr)_{(\mu,\lambda)}\, M_\mu^* ,$$
where $M_\mu^*$ denotes the ambient orthonormal dual frame of the standard
basis. The $G_{\mathrm{sym}}^*(\lambda)$ are the **ambient upper coordinates**
of the basic module: they are the unique elements of the basic subspace
$(M_{\mathrm{sym}})_w\subseteq V_w$ characterized weightwise by $B(G_{\mathrm{sym}}^*(\lambda), G_{\mathrm{sym}}(\lambda')) = \delta_{\lambda\lambda'}$,
and are viewed in the ambient standard frame; adding a vector of the
$B$-orthogonal complement in $V_w$ gives other ambient representatives with
the same pairings. The coefficients
$e_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q) := (D_{\mathrm{rect}}H^{-1})_{(\mu,\lambda)}$ lie in
$\mathbb{Q}(q)$ but need not be Laurent integral or polynomial. They are
coordinates in the ambient space and not a "standard basis of the basic
module"; the exact integral upper basis is the transported upper global basis of
[[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]], whose
restricted graded $A$-dual lattice is free weightwise and perfectly paired with
the basic lower $A$-span, while no lower-$A$ selfduality, no $A$-unit $H$ and no
full algebraic duality in infinite rank is implied. The restriction of $B$ to the basic module equals the normalized transported
contravariant form (proved in step 4.2), so these are the same upper vectors
viewed in the ambient standard frame and in their own integral dual lattice.
Upper bar is the adjoint bar
$\psi^\vee$ with its own dual infinity chart and weighted upper operators, not
the ordinary lower bar.

**The full ambient case.** On the whole Fock space the analogous matrix
$D_{\mathrm{full}}$, with columns the $G(\mu)$ over all partitions and rows the
standard shapes, is unitriangular (diagonal $1$, in $q\mathbb{Z}[q]$ below the
diagonal), and the dual matrix with respect to $B$ is
$$D_{\mathrm{full}}^{-\mathsf{t}},$$
which is Laurent integral because the inverse of a unitriangular matrix with
entries in $\mathbb{Z}[q]$ has entries in $\mathbb{Z}[q]$.

**A worked instance.** At $e = 2$ the restricted shape $\lambda = (1,1)$ has
$G_{\mathrm{sym}}(1,1) = M_{1,1} + q\,M_{2}$, so $D_{\mathrm{rect}}$ has the
single column $(q,1)^{\mathsf{t}}$, $H = 1 + q^2$, and
$$G_{\mathrm{sym}}^*(1,1) = \frac{M_{1,1}^* + q\,M_2^*}{1+q^2} = \frac{M_{1,1} + q\,M_2}{1+q^2},$$
an explicit ambient coordinate that is rational but not Laurent integral:
$1 + q^2$ is not a unit of $\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]$. No specialization of the $d$
to decomposition numbers of Hecke algebras is asserted here without the
separate correct Hecke parameter hypotheses.
after_row.strategy: Transport the lower Fock basis by the linear transpose-label map J, preserving q; obtain the exact coefficient identity, symmetric dominance direction, same-core and full reflected-weight support. Work weightwise with the rectangular lower-column matrix D and ambient orthonormal form. D(0) has distinct coordinate columns, so H=D^tD satisfies H(0)=I and is field invertible; DH^-1 gives the unique upper vectors inside the basic subspace, with whole-ambient representatives differing by its orthogonal complement. Compute the e=2 rational coordinates and the full ambient transpose-inverse matrix separately. The finite node-count identity Nright+Nleft=N(lambda)-1 proves sigma-adjointness of the orthonormal form; normalized highest-weight form uniqueness identifies its basic restriction with the transported QG form. Thus these upper vectors form the restricted integral dual basis with perfect pairing, while rational standard coordinates imply neither lower-A selfduality nor an A-unit Gram matrix. Transport the exact adjoint upper bar, dual charts and weighted operators; preserve all linear/semilinear and Hecke-parameter boundaries.

before_row.title: Standard Fock vectors expand in the upper global basis
before_row.statement:
Use the actual symmetric model M_mu=|mu transpose>, the basic field subspace V spanned by the restricted lower vectors G(lambda)=sum_mu d_(lambda,mu)(q) M_mu, and the bilinear form B(M_mu,M_nu)=delta_(mu,nu). Define the STANDARD COORDINATE FUNCTIONAL Std_mu in the RESTRICTED integral weight dual of the lower lattice by Std_mu(x)=B(x,M_mu). The restriction of B to V is nondegenerate; identify its field dual with V and denote by pi(M_mu) the vector representing Std_mu, equivalently the B-orthogonal projection of M_mu onto V. This is the definition of pi used below, not an undeclared projection from a generic upper-basis definition. If G^*(lambda) is the B/form-dual upper vector, then
$$Std_mu=pi(M_mu)=sum_{lambda restricted} d_(lambda,mu)(q) G^*(lambda).$$
At each content the restricted Std_lambda form an A-basis of the UPPER dual lattice, by the restricted dominance-unitriangular coefficient minor. The full family of raw M_mu is the basis of the ambient standard lattice; the full projected family Std_mu is generally redundant. Pi need not land in the LOWER integral lattice. In e2, G_11=M_11+q M_2 and G_11^*=(M_11+q M_2)/(1+q²), exhibiting the possible field denominator. The sums at fixed content are finite. Choice is inherited only from the declared global-basis suppliers.
before_row.strategy: At a fixed content let D have row mu and column lambda equal to d_(lambda,mu); its columns are the lower vectors in the standard basis. The restricted square minor is dominance-unitriangular, hence the columns are independent over Q(q). The Gram matrix is H=D^t D. A nonzero real specialization of q away from the finitely many denominators preserves the unitriangular minor, so those real columns have positive definite Gram matrix. Therefore det H is not the zero rational function. This proves nondegeneracy and defines the field orthogonal projection. For x=sum_lambda a_lambda G(lambda), Std_mu(x)=sum_lambda a_lambda d_(lambda,mu), proving integral values on the lower A-lattice. Evaluate on each G(lambda): the field/form-dual basis yields the displayed coefficient expansion. The restricted coefficient minor has determinant1 over A, so the corresponding Std_lambda form a basis of the upper dual; no inverse of1+q² is asserted to be a Laurent unit. Raw standard M_mu remain a basis of the ambient lattice, whereas projected standards can repeat the same upper weight space. The node polarization B(F_i x,y)=B(x,q^-1 K_i E_i y) and its inverse-adjoint formula show that V and V-perpendicular are invariant; pi therefore commutes with the field quantum action. In the symmetric linear-J convention E counts minus ABOVE, so E_i Std_mu=sum_remA q^(-d^A(mu)) Std_(mu minus A). This is exactly the canonical recursion used by the later Specht comparison, with no switch to the KK action. The actual original quantum reviewer supplied these guarded interfaces; no quantum9/23 source is altered. Choice only as inherited.

before_row.title: Graded decomposition numbers equal canonical-basis coefficients in characteristic zero
before_row.statement: In branch (C0) of the regime of [[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], for every partition $\mu$ with content $\alpha$ and every $\lambda\in RP_\alpha$, the graded composition multiplicity satisfies $$[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]_q=d_{\lambda,\mu}(q),$$ where $d_{\lambda,\mu}$ is the level-one global-basis transition polynomial of [[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]; equivalently $[S(\mu)]=\sum_{\lambda\in RP_\alpha}d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)[D(\lambda)]$ in $G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$, and $d_{\lambda,\mu}=0$ unless $\lambda\unlhd\mu$. Specializing $q=1$ gives Ariki's ungraded decomposition-number theorem $[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]=d_{\lambda,\mu}(1)$. Choice is inherited only through the QG-8 global-basis suppliers.
before_row.strategy: Apply the transported isomorphism $\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}$ to the class of $S(\mu)$: by [[thm-graded-specht-classes-realize-standard-fock-vectors]] it equals $S_\mu$, and by [[lem-standard-fock-vectors-expand-in-the-upper-global-basis]] $S_\mu=\sum_{\lambda}d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)G^*(\lambda)$ with the same coefficients as the lower expansion. By [[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]] (2) the vectors $G^*(\lambda)$ are the images of the simple classes $[D(\lambda)]$, so applying $(\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke})^{-1}$ yields $[S(\mu)]=\sum_\lambda d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)[D(\lambda)]$; the composition multiplicities are read off because the simple classes form a basis of the free $A$-module $G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$ ([[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] (2)). The dominance vanishing is the support statement of [[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]. The $q=1$ specialization is the forgetful map of [[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]], and the ungraded statement is [BK 2009, Theorem 5.9] (Ariki). This is [BK 2009, Theorem 5.14 and Corollary 5.15], with [Kleshchev, Theorem 9.9] as the independent treatment. No new choice.

after_row.title: Graded Specht heads classify the graded simple modules
after_row.statement:
In the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], for
$\lambda\in RP_\alpha$ the graded Specht module $S(\lambda)$ of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]] has irreducible
head, denoted $\dot D(\lambda)$, and
$\dot D(\lambda)^\circledast\cong\dot D(\lambda)$. Moreover:

1. the modules $\{\dot D(\lambda)\langle m\rangle:\lambda\in RP_\alpha,\ m\in\mathbb Z\}$
are a complete set of pairwise non-isomorphic graded simple
$R^\Lambda_\alpha$-modules (equivalently, of $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ with the
transported grading);

2. in $G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$ one has
$[S(\lambda)]=[\dot D(\lambda)]+(\ast)$ if $\lambda$ is restricted and
$[S(\lambda)]=(\ast)$ otherwise, where $(\ast)$ is an $A$-linear combination of
$[\dot D(\mu)]$'s with $\mu\lhd\lambda$; consequently
$[S(\mu):\dot D(\lambda)]_q\ne0$ implies $\lambda\unlhd\mu$, and
$[S(\lambda):\dot D(\lambda)]_q=1$;

3. in branch (C0), $\dot D(\lambda)\cong D(\lambda)$, the normalized simple
with crystal label $\lambda$ of
[[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] (4);
separately, after forgetting the grading and converting the ordinary right
modules through star, $\dot D(\lambda)\cong(D_{\rm DJ}^{\lambda'})^{\theta}$ by
`thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell`. Thus the
conjugate $e$-regular ordinary label occurs with the explicit
sign-automorphism pullback, which reflects residue content and is not an
untwisted same-block identification. The ordinary module dictionary and radical
comparison hold in both field branches; the crystal-label comparison in this
part is the stated (C0) assertion.

Parts (1) and (2) hold in both branches (C0) and (CP); part (3) is stated in
branch (C0), the branch of the decomposition theorem it consumes. The branch
(CP) analogue of (3) is the identification [BK 2009, Theorem 5.18] and is NOT
asserted here. Choice is inherited only through the cited transported
global-basis suppliers, as recorded in the contract.
after_row.strategy: Apply the actual finite-cell classification of nonzero-form heads and factor ordering. Invert the restricted unitriangular transition minor to express an unrestricted Specht class in strictly dominated restricted Specht classes; cellular factor ordering excludes a nonzero-form head at that unrestricted label. All distinguished labels are thus restricted, and comparing the simple-class Grothendieck rank with the restricted Specht basis count proves every restricted label is distinguished. The local cellular diagonal and smaller-factor clauses supply the head expansion. In C0 compare the crystal-labelled and head-labelled unitriangular expansions by finite dominance induction. Use finite duality and the leading coefficient to fix the zero duality shift, and independently retain the actual signed-conjugate ordinary Specht/form dictionary across both branches. No new Choice is introduced.
